VBO:0200391.summary: The Cretan Hound tends to be gentle and affectionate with its people, yet persistent and daring on a hare trail. It works by both sight and scent across rocky ground, often hunting alone or in a pair. The breed standard notes a distinctive, fairly quiet voice when the dog sights or pursues quarry.
VBO:0200391.shortDescription: Gentle with its people and persistent on rocky hare trails, the Cretan Hound hunts by both sight and scent.

sources.title: Cretan Hound breed standard (Kennel Club of Greece, 2003; Cretan Hound breed-club archive)
sources.evidence: Temperament and abilities: gentle, affectionate and devoted at home; on the hunt persistent, brave and tireless. General characteristics: pursues hare or wild rabbit alone or in pairs, using sight and scent across rocky terrain, and gives an idiomatic low voice on sighting or chasing quarry. No prehistoric-continuity claim used.

VBO:0200496.summary: English Shepherds often meet farm work with calm independence while staying closely tuned to their handler. They can gather or drive stock in an upright, loose-eyed style, choosing the pressure the task needs rather than fixing on one approach. Generations of all-purpose farm work also called on them to guard the home and deal with vermin.
VBO:0200496.shortDescription: Calm and independent on the farm, the English Shepherd handles stock with a loose eye and stays attuned to its handler.

sources.title: English Shepherd Club breed standard
sources.evidence: Introduction: generations as all-purpose working farm dogs, herding/protecting stock, dispatching vermin and guarding home. Working Characteristics: upright loose-eyed stock work; gather or drive as needed; discerning pressure; independent ability combined with desire to work in partnership; capable of resting quietly between chores.

VBO:0200990.summary: Patterdale Terriers are bold, active dogs with a strong prey drive and a marked willingness to work with their people. Developed among northern England's fell terriers, they followed quarry into tight burrows and held it at bay; their work was tied to controlling vermin around sheep country.
VBO:0200990.shortDescription: Bold and keen to work, this northern English earth terrier follows quarry into tight burrows.
VBO:0200990.historicalRoots: Northern English Fell Terrier developed for underground vermin work in sheep country.

sources.title: United Kennel Club: Patterdale Terrier breed standard
sources.evidence: UKC History traces northern England Fell Terrier ancestry, sheep-country vermin control and underground work; General Appearance explains tight-burrow pursuit and holding quarry at bay; Characteristics calls the breed extremely courageous, active, strong in prey drive and willing to work.

VBO:0201142.summary: Romanian Raven Shepherd Dogs tend to be calm and attached to their own people, while reserved with strangers. In the southern Carpathians they guarded flocks and households, and their deep bark could carry over a great distance. The breed's name comes from its predominantly black coat.
VBO:0201142.shortDescription: Calm with its own people and reserved with strangers, this Carpathian flock guardian has a far-carrying bark.
VBO:0201142.historicalRoots: Southern Carpathian and sub-Carpathian flock and household guardian of Romania.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 373: Romanian Raven Shepherd Dog
sources.evidence: FCI 373 historical summary locates the breed in the Meridional/southern Carpathians, says it guarded flocks and households, and derives Raven from predominantly black coat; temperament says balanced/calm, attached to masters, diffident with strangers, deep bark audible at great distance.

VBO:0200212.summary: Boxers are often playful and friendly, with a self-assured steadiness behind their lively energy. They tend to be deeply attached to their people and watchful around strangers. Their immediate ancestors, the Brabant Bullenbeissers, held game brought to bay by hounds until the huntsman arrived.
VBO:0200212.shortDescription: Playful and people-focused, the Boxer often pairs a friendly spirit with calm confidence and watchfulness.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 144 — Deutscher Boxer
sources.evidence: Behaviour/Temperament supports playful, friendly, steady, devoted and watchful character; Historical Summary documents Brabant Bullenbeisser hunting task.

VBO:0200014.summary: Alapaha Blue Blood Bulldogs tend to be confident and alert, with a guardian's watchfulness and a wary response to strangers. Bred for protection and family companionship, they are also expected to respond to training and commands, placing cooperation alongside physical strength.
VBO:0200014.shortDescription: A watchful, confident guardian that stays responsive to its handler and close to its family.
VBO:0200014.historicalRoots: Southern American guardian and functional bulldog heritage.

sources.title: Alapaha Bulldog Association: Breed Standard
sources.evidence: Association standard identifies guardian/protector/family-companion use and a confident, alert, assertive dog responsive to training and commands, distrustful of strangers; tail and ear standards support morphology.

VBO:0200488.summary: English Cocker Spaniels are gentle and affectionate, yet exuberant when a scent catches them. Their bustling movement and fearless way through heavy cover come from work flushing woodcock; the breed’s name comes from that bird. The standard describes an ever-wagging tail, especially as they follow scent.
VBO:0200488.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate, this merry spaniel was bred to flush woodcock from dense cover.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 5 — English Cocker Spaniel
sources.evidence: FCI 5 pp. 2–4 documents gentle, affectionate, merry and exuberant temperament, an ever-wagging tail especially when following a scent, woodcock-flushing history, and black among solid colours.

VBO:0201003.summary: Perro Majoreros tend to be loyal and strongly territorial, warm with familiar people but wary of strangers. On Fuerteventura they directed livestock without harming it and guarded property; their sure-footed movement over rough lava ground was part of that working life.
VBO:0201003.shortDescription: Loyal to familiar people and wary of strangers, this Fuerteventura worker herded stock and watched property.
VBO:0201003.historicalRoots: Fuerteventura livestock driving and property guarding on rough volcanic terrain.

sources.title: Real Sociedad Canina de España: Majorero standard No. 402
sources.evidence: Sections III, XV and XVI describe loyalty/territorial watchfulness, warmth toward familiar people and reserve toward strangers, stock direction without harming livestock, guarding property; section II describes sure-footed movement across lava terrain.

VBO:0200572.summary: German Pinschers are lively, self-assured and even-tempered, with the alertness to serve as watchdogs while remaining close family companions. The smooth-coated pinscher appeared in German stud records by 1880 and shares its ancestry with the rough-coated line that became the Schnauzer; black and tan is one of its recognized colors.
VBO:0200572.shortDescription: Lively and self-assured, this black-and-tan Pinscher brings watchfulness to family life.
VBO:0200572.historicalRoots: German smooth-coated pinscher recorded by 1880; black-and-tan color variety.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 184: German Pinscher
sources.evidence: FCI 184 identifies lively, spirited, self-assured and even-tempered watch/companion character, German Stud Book mention in 1880, common ancestry with the Schnauzer, black-and-tan markings and natural sabre/sickle tail. No color-specific character claim.

VBO:0200022.summary: Alopekis dogs are quick, attentive little farm companions that can raise an alarm and remain protective of their familiar group. This Greek landrace has also been used to control vermin and guide livestock, several tasks performed by a compact, agile dog rather than a single-purpose specialist.
VBO:0200022.shortDescription: This quick Greek farm dog sounds a warning, controls vermin and helps guide livestock.
VBO:0200022.historicalRoots: Small Greek landrace used for general farm utility and companionship.

sources.title: O.M.M.A.: Alopekis breed page
sources.evidence: O.M.M.A. Alopekis breed page documents small Greek landrace identity distinct from Kokoni, wirehaired form, warning/protective behavior, vermin control and stock guidance; omit prehistoric continuity assertions.

VBO:0201024.summary: Plummer Terriers tend to be active, alert and tenacious, yet affectionate with family and familiar people. Brian Plummer developed the breed in the 1960s for practical terrier work; its breed club still emphasizes searching for and controlling vermin both above and below ground.
VBO:0201024.shortDescription: Active and tenacious in terrier work, the Plummer is also affectionate with familiar people.
VBO:0201024.historicalRoots: Modern British working terrier developed by Brian Plummer from the 1960s.

sources.title: Plummer Terrier Club of Great Britain: Breed History
sources.evidence: Club history credits Brian Plummer with development from the 1960s for hunting and other practical terrier work.

sources.title: Plummer Terrier Club of Great Britain: Breed Standard
sources.evidence: General Character says active, adaptable, courageous and tenacious, affectionate/loyal with family and friends, alert without excessive aggression; standard emphasizes hunting vermin above and below ground.

VBO:0200606.summary: Giant Schnauzers tend to be even-tempered, loyal and self-assured, with keen senses and an eagerness for work. In southern Germany they originally drove cattle, and the breed was formally recognized as a working dog in 1925. Their endurance and trainability remain part of the character described for the breed.
VBO:0200606.shortDescription: Even-tempered and self-assured, this loyal German worker began as a southern cattle driver.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 181 — Giant Schnauzer
sources.evidence: FCI 181 pp. 2–3 documents even temperament, loyalty, senses, intelligence, trainability and endurance; Southern German cattle-driving history and 1925 work recognition; pp. 5–6 permit pepper/salt coat.

VBO:0200398.summary: The Cursinu can be calm at home yet lively at work, strongly attached to its person while remaining wary of strangers. Corsican farmers used it to bring back stray free-ranging animals rather than drive an entire herd; later the same adaptable dog found a place in scent hunting through the island's rough cover.
VBO:0200398.shortDescription: Calm at home and lively in action, this Corsican worker once brought strays back to the herd.
VBO:0200398.historicalRoots: Corsican stock work and later scent-hunting heritage.

sources.title: Société Centrale Canine: Cursinu standard
sources.evidence: Société Centrale Canine Cursinu standard: docile/loyal/attached, wary strangers, quiet at home and lively in action; retrieved straying free-range stock rather than driving whole herds; later scent-hunting role in Corsica; fawn brindle and thick complete tail.

VBO:0201334.summary: Tamaskan Dogs are generally friendly and outgoing, although some meet new people with a little reserve and can work independently. Their northern sled-dog heritage shows in an active, willing worker able to pull light loads at a moderate pace over short distances.
VBO:0201334.shortDescription: Friendly and willing to work, this northern sled-dog descendant may be reserved at first.
VBO:0201334.historicalRoots: Modern northern sled-dog-derived breed represented by the Tamaskan Dog Register.

sources.title: Tamaskan Dog Register: Breed Standard
sources.evidence: TDR temperament describes friendly, outgoing, good-natured dogs; some are initially reserved but easily won over and some independent. General appearance/utilization describes northern sled-dog heritage, capable adaptable working, light loads at moderate pace over short distances, tracking and service work.

VBO:0200677.summary: Hovawarts are often even-natured and devoted to family, while remaining alert and protective. Their name comes from old German words for a yard or estate and a guardian, a clue to the work behind the breed. Beginning in 1922, breeders developed the modern Hovawart from farm dogs and related working stock; its keen nose also suits tracking and rescue work.
VBO:0200677.shortDescription: Even-natured and family-devoted, the Hovawart carries an old German farm-guardian name and a keen nose.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 190 — Hovawart
sources.evidence: FCI 190 pp. 2–3 documents good-natured/even/protective/family devotion, scenting, tracking and rescue; name etymology and 1922 reconstruction; pp. 5–6 distinguish blond variety.

VBO:0201201.summary: The Segugio dell'Appennino has a strong hunting drive and can work closely with its handler while showing initiative on the trail. Bred for hare country in the Apennines, these hounds search and follow scent across steep ground, sometimes alone and sometimes in pairs.
VBO:0201201.shortDescription: Driven to follow hare scent through Apennine hills, this hound works alone or in a pair with its handler.
VBO:0201201.historicalRoots: Italian Apennine hare-hunting hound used on mountainous ground.

sources.title: Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana: Segugio dell'Appennino
sources.evidence: ENCI describes strong hunting drive, a close handler bond with independent finding and pursuit, hare hunting through Apennine mountains and work alone or in pairs.

VBO:0200573.summary: German Pinschers are spirited and intelligent without losing the even temper of a companion. Their endurance and quick attention also suit the breed's traditional watchdog role. This self-colored red variety belongs to the same smooth-coated German line recorded in the stud book by 1880, alongside the black-and-tan dogs.
VBO:0200573.shortDescription: Spirited, intelligent and even-tempered, this red Pinscher has a German watchdog heritage.
VBO:0200573.historicalRoots: German smooth-coated pinscher recorded by 1880; self-colored red variety.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 184: German Pinscher
sources.evidence: FCI 184 gives lively, spirited, intelligent, enduring and even-tempered watch/companion character; smooth-coated German Pinscher entered stud records by 1880; self-colored deer red to dark red-brown is an exact recognized variety. No color-specific behavior claim.

VBO:0200433.summary: Danish Spitz dogs tend to be affectionate and sociable with familiar people, but they may be reserved and vocal when someone new approaches. Long valued around Jutland farms as companions and watchdogs, they generally stay close to home and have a relatively modest hunting urge.
VBO:0200433.shortDescription: Affectionate with family and watchful of newcomers, this Danish farm companion tends to stay near home.
VBO:0200433.historicalRoots: Danish and Jutland farm companion and watchdog heritage.

sources.title: Danish Kennel Club: Danish Spitz breed page
sources.evidence: Danish Kennel Club breed page describes friendliness with known people, affectionate family attachment, mild reserve/alert barking around strangers, farm/watch/companion history, modest hunting drive and staying near home.

VBO:0200767.summary: King Charles Spaniels tend to be gentle, affectionate and somewhat reserved, with a happy, intelligent manner. These English Toy Spaniels descended from small gundogs, then became treasured companions in England and on the Continent. Their name recalls a dog favoured by Charles II; later crosses with Eastern toy dogs helped shape their distinctive face.
VBO:0200767.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate with a little reserve, this English Toy Spaniel recalls a royal companion.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 128 — King Charles Spaniel
sources.evidence: FCI 128 pp. 2–3 describes happy, intelligent, reserved, gentle and affectionate character, Charles II naming and English toy companion history; pp. 3–4 define domed head/short muzzle, separate relationship to Cavalier, Blenheim pattern.

VBO:0200933.summary: Nenets Herding Laikas tend to be lively and friendly, eager to learn yet able to decide for themselves. Their strong inborn herding instinct developed around moving reindeer in Russia’s far north, where a close bond with people was also part of the breed’s working life.
VBO:0200933.shortDescription: Lively and independent-minded, this far-northern Russian herder works closely with people and reindeer.
VBO:0200933.historicalRoots: Nenets reindeer-herding dog of the Russian far north.

sources.title: Russian Cynological Federation: Nenets Reindeer Herding Laika recognition and standard
sources.evidence: RKF standard behavior describes lively, friendly, trainable, initiative-taking, independently deciding dog with a strongly developed innate herding instinct; describes a companion following its person. Historical/use section locates reindeer herding in far northern Russia.

VBO:0200899.summary: Miniature Schnauzers bring fearless alertness and stamina to the watchful companion role. Around 1900 in the Frankfurt area, breeders shaped rough-haired small pinschers into a miniature counterpart of the Schnauzer, seeking the larger breed’s characteristic qualities in a smaller dog.
VBO:0200899.shortDescription: Fearless and alert, this Miniature Schnauzer traces its roots to small rough-haired dogs around Frankfurt.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 183: Miniature Schnauzer
sources.evidence: Historical summary describes development around Frankfurt/Main circa 1900 from rough-haired Zwergpinscher toward a small Schnauzer type; temperament section gives intelligence, fearlessness, endurance and alertness, including watch/companion roles; coat section separately recognizes pure black with black undercoat.

VBO:0200976.summary: Olde English Bulldogges are confident and friendly dogs with an alert, animated manner. A breeding project begun in 1971 set out to restore the agility and working ability of a Regency-period bulldog; the UKC describes today’s breed first as a companion while retaining scope for varied work.
VBO:0200976.shortDescription: Confident and friendly, this animated bulldog arose from a 1971 project to restore working ability.
VBO:0200976.historicalRoots: Modern American reconstruction begun in 1971 to evoke a functional Regency-era bulldog.

sources.title: United Kennel Club: Olde English Bulldogge breed standard
sources.evidence: UKC Characteristics describes confident, friendly and alert disposition with animated, expressive manner. History identifies a 1971 program to return the bulldog to Regency-period appearance and function; describes the modern breed first as companion with working and service ability.

VBO:0200900.summary: Miniature Schnauzers tend to be alert, fearless and enduring companions. Early breeders around Frankfurt had to work through dogs with varied sizes, shapes and coat textures to establish a small dog with the distinctive qualities of the larger Schnauzer.
VBO:0200900.shortDescription: Alert and enduring, this Miniature Schnauzer brings a watchful temperament to companion life.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 183: Miniature Schnauzer
sources.evidence: FCI history traces Frankfurt-area development from rough-haired Zwergpinscher circa 1900; temperament describes alertness, fearlessness and endurance with watch/companion roles; coat section separately recognizes pure white with white undercoat. Character claims are breed-wide, not color-specific.

VBO:0201150.summary: Russian Spaniels tend to be friendly with people, energetic in the field and responsive to a handler. Developed for bird hunting, they search cover, flush game and retrieve it across varied terrain; their work calls for close cooperation as well as the stamina to keep moving.
VBO:0201150.shortDescription: Friendly and energetic, this bird dog works close to its handler to search, flush and retrieve game.
VBO:0201150.historicalRoots: Russian sporting spaniel developed to search, flush and retrieve birds across varied terrain.

sources.title: Russian Spaniel Club: Breed Standard
sources.evidence: Club standard describes friendly disposition, energetic close work and trainability.

sources.title: Russian Spaniel Club: About the Breed
sources.evidence: Club history/use explains bird-hunting development, searching, flushing and retrieving in varied terrain.

VBO:0200888.summary: Miniature Bull Terriers are spirited and courageous, often pairing a fun-loving streak with an obstinate side. The smaller Bull Terrier type was known in the early 1800s, then fell from the Kennel Club register in 1918. Enthusiasts formed a club and revived the breed in 1938.
VBO:0200888.shortDescription: Spirited and fun-loving, this smaller Bull Terrier survived an early decline through a 1938 revival.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 359 — Miniature Bull Terrier
sources.evidence: FCI 359 pp. 2–3 describes spirit, courage, fun-loving disposition and obstinacy, early-19th-century type, 1918 register removal and 1938 club revival; p. 5 permits pure white coat.
